title: -Os miscompile of hcs08_vformat: %u consumes 4 bytes instead of 2
status: OPEN - localized, root cause not found
severity: high - silently wrong output from correct C; no diagnostic
found_by: running the HCS08 SDK's printf on real silicon (MC9S08AW60)

symptom.description: In a printf-family call, a %u (or %d) conversion reads a 32-bit value where it should read 16, so it swallows two adjacent 16-bit varargs and prints them as one. Conversions before it are correct.

observed.note: 26 == (0 << 16) | 26, i.e. one clean 32-bit read spanning both args
1720980 == 0x001A46D4; 0x1A == 26 sits in the HIGH half. %s and %c are CORRECT.

symptom.stability: The FIRST wrong conversion is deterministic across builds. Later ones vary (17044, 17123, 17255) - that is reading uninitialised stack past the last argument.

key_insight.statement: %s and %c are correct and only %u is wrong, so the argument cursor advances properly and then the %u conversion itself over-reads.
key_insight.why_it_matters: This is NOT a va_start/va_list offset bug. Three reproducers were built against that wrong model and none reproduced. Any new reproducer must make the *conversion* over-read, not the cursor start wrong.
key_insight.corollary: More than one local is corrupt: with HCS08FuseCompareBranch disabled, `width` also came back garbage (output became '[' + 20 spaces). Points at register allocation or spill placement, not a mis-taken branch.

trigger_conditions.optimization: -Os FAILS, -O1 PASSES. -O0 cannot be tested: frame reaches SP+277 vs the 256-byte ceiling and the backend correctly refuses.
trigger_conditions.source_config: Fails only when HCS08_PRINTF_LONG=1, i.e. when the 32-bit converter is present in the same function as the 16-bit one. HCS08_PRINTF_LONG=0 passes.
trigger_conditions.function: hcs08_vformat in hcs08-sdk/lib/libc/printf/fmt.c - large, variadic, four near-identical inlined conversion loops (%d and %u each split narrow/wide).

established_facts.evidence: hcs08_vformat has exactly 2x 'udiv i16' and 2x 'udiv i32'. Both narrow/wide selections are 'icmp eq i8 %longs.0, 0' against the loop-header phi - right value, right point.
established_facts.conclusion: Middle end and the C source are both exonerated. This is a backend bug.

established_facts.fact: The machine code keeps the right shape.
established_facts.evidence: 2 'jsr __udivhi3' sites and 2 'jsr __udivsi3' sites at -Os with LONG=1.
established_facts.conclusion: No narrow conversion site was rewritten into a wide one.

established_facts.fact: The narrow blocks are reachable only by fall-through.
established_facts.evidence: Nothing branches INTO .LBB1_84 or .LBB1_99 except their own loop-back edges.
established_facts.conclusion: Legal, but this is where to look: verify the fall-through predecessor is guarded by the longs==0 test.

established_facts.fact: Frames are nowhere near the 8-bit displacement ceiling.
established_facts.evidence: hcs08_vformat frame = 74 bytes at -Os/LONG=1, 49 at -Os/LONG=0, 77 at -O1/LONG=1. Largest n,sp displacement observed 0x51.
established_facts.conclusion: Nothing wraps. Note the WORKING -O1 build has a BIGGER frame than the failing -Os build, so frame size is not the variable.

eliminated.method: %s and %c through the same cursor are correct; a noinline callee consuming a va_list against snprintf's exact signature is correct; f(fmt,...), f(fmt,int,...) and f(buf,n,fmt,...) all correct.
declared it volatile, forcing it to memory
HCS08_PRINTF_LONG also shrinks FMT_DIGITS 12->8, so the passing build was a confounded two-variable change. Forced FMT_DIGITS=8 while keeping the wide path.
eliminated.result: fails byte-for-byte identically - it is the wide path, not the frame

eliminated.suspect: Machine tail merging of the four similar loops
eliminated.result: still fails (was the leading theory; it is wrong)

eliminated.method: -mllvm -hcs08-no-fuse-compare-branch (flag added in commit 508bfd6e3838 for this purpose)
eliminated.result: still fails, but DIFFERENTLY - `width` also corrupt. Informative: multiple locals are wrong.

eliminated.suspect: va_arg for 2-byte and 4-byte types in one variadic function
eliminated.method: minimal variadic fn with va_arg(unsigned int) and va_arg(unsigned long) on runtime-selected paths, run on silicon

eliminated.suspect: Branch selection between two inlined loops, in isolation
eliminated.method: 25-line fn with a narrow and a wide conversion loop selected on a runtime flag, run on silicon
eliminated.result: correct (returns "26") - does not reproduce; note it used no varargs, which was the flaw

workarounds.cost: %ld truncates to 16 bits instead of corrupting following args; %u and %d correct

debug_plan.note: Steps are ordered cheapest-first. Steps 1-2 need no hardware.

steps.title: Diff the machine pass pipeline between -O1 and -Os
steps.why: This is the one mechanical step left; everything else has been guesswork. -O1 passes and -Os fails on identical source.
how: for O in -O1 -Os; do $B/clang -target hcs08 $O -ffreestanding -std=c11 -fno-builtin -DHCS08_PRINTF_LONG=1 -I$S/include -I$S/devices/aw60/include -mllvm -print-after-all -S -o /dev/null $S/lib/libc/printf/fmt.c 2>/tmp/pa$O.txt; done
diff the two, restricted to hcs08_vformat
steps.looking_for: the first pass after which the %u path stops loading two bytes (i.e. a 16-bit load becomes 32-bit, or the narrow block loses its guard)

steps.title: Check the fall-through guard into the narrow blocks
steps.why: Nothing branches into .LBB1_84/.LBB1_99 except loop-backs, so correctness depends entirely on their fall-through predecessor being guarded by longs==0.
how: locate the blocks containing 'jsr __udivhi3' and walk their predecessors

steps.title: Bisect the -Os-only machine passes
steps.why: Three target-specific passes are excluded; the remaining delta is generic -Os machine passes (MachineSink, MachineCSE, MachineBlockPlacement, RegAllocGreedy heuristics).
how: disable candidates individually with -mllvm flags at -Os until it passes

steps.title: Reduce with the corrected model
steps.why: All three previous reproducers assumed a cursor offset. The real shape is: cursor correct for N conversions, then one conversion over-reads.
how: start from fmt.c and delete downward, keeping a variadic caller, four inlined conversion loops, and a switch
verify each step on silicon - ucsim CANNOT be used, see gotchas

gotchas.trap: ucsim results are worthless for this bug
gotchas.detail: ucsim does not implement ldhx/sthx n,sp (0x9E FE/FF), which is exactly the 16-bit stack-argument path varargs use. It reported a DIFFERENT wrong answer than the part, and reports this failing even when the part runs it correctly. test/target/t_pf2.c is marked SILICON_ONLY for this reason.

gotchas.trap: The SDK's 370 host printf tests pass throughout, before and after
gotchas.detail: They use the host libc as an oracle. The host's int is 32-bit, so a converter reading 32 where it should read 16 is simply correct there. The host oracle is structurally blind to target argument layout.

gotchas.trap: -O0 cannot be used as a control
gotchas.detail: hcs08_vformat's frame reaches SP+277 against the 256-byte ceiling and the backend refuses. That refusal is correct and unrelated to this bug. A build script that does not check for a failed compile will silently test a stale .o and report a false PASS - this happened once.
A grep filter listing bne/beq/jmp but not bcc made a correct narrow loop look like it had no exit test. Dump whole blocks before concluding.
It gates the wide converter AND changes FMT_DIGITS 12->8, hence the frame. Any experiment toggling it is confounded unless FMT_DIGITS is pinned.

llvm.note: build with ninja inside `toolbox run -c fedora`; make/ninja/cmake are not on the host

sdk.reproducer: test/target/t_pf2.c (has the full narrative in its trailing comment)

silicon.part: MC9S08AW60 on a Valco/VICI UA display board
silicon.bus_clock_note: MEASURED: with --reset-into-bdm the BDC reports CLKSW set and 4.000 MHz, which is the bus. Do not use 3888000 - that is the STOCK firmware's clock, which configures the ICG; SDK crt0 does not.
silicon.programmer: Glasgow revC3, applet debug-hcs08 at /var/home/atomicdog/repo/glasgow (branch wip-applet.debug.hcs08)
silicon.wiring: BKGD=A0, RESET=A1, ground to BDM pin 2, port A at 3.3 V. Serial (if needed): board TX -> A3, board RX -> A2, uart applet with --rx A3 --tx A2 -b 9600.
quirks: After `program` the PC sits in the applet's FLASH routine in the high-page register block (~$180E), NOT at the reset vector. You must --reset-into-bdm before `run` or you execute the register file as code.
RAM survives a reset, which is what lets silicon.py poison it before running.
